snippet.title: One of the worst civil engineering failures in American history
snippet.description: In 1922, William Mulholland began building the St. Francis Dam to create a reservoir for the Los Angeles–Owens River aqueduct. To meet LA's growing water needs, he decided to increase the height of the dam by 20 feet — without widening the base. This on-the-fly change would have catastrophic consequences.

snippet.description:

snippet.title: Engineering Disasters Designers Never Expected | Engineering by Catastrophe | National Geographic UK
snippet.description:
From collapsing bridges and swaying skyscrapers to the future of nuclear safety, engineering at the highest level means preparing for the unimaginable.

After the Baltimore bridge disaster, experts reveal how suspension bridges like the 1915 Çanakkale Bridge are designed with colossal underwater defence systems capable of absorbing devastating impacts.

In Boston, a sleek glass skyscraper earned the nickname “The Plywood Palace” after massive windows began crashing onto the streets below, exposing dangerous flaws in the building’s design.

And in Flamanville, engineers develop next-generation nuclear reactors with passive safety systems designed to contain disaster even in a total meltdown scenario.

From wind tunnels and bridge foundations to nuclear containment systems, these are the hidden engineering battles shaping the modern world.

snippet.description:

In this gripping documentary, we count down the top 10 bridge and tunnel disasters, examining the breathtaking scale of these tragedies and the lessons learned from each one.
